This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed
investing to full service wealth management, all in one place. No matter your investing
goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Life from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston. Flights are suspended at the main
airport in the capital of Saudi Arabia. Officials in Riyadh say a missile attack inside a passenger
terminal on Saturday killed at least 12 people and wounded hundreds of others, some critically.
NPR's Ayyeb Etrawi reports from Dubai.
This is the deadliest attack on the capital of Riyadh since 2015, when Saudi Arabia led
a coalition of countries into war in Yemen against the Iran-backed Houthis. Prior to
Saturday's attack, the Houthis had already hit Riyadh's airport twice this week, piercing
through Saudi Arabia's air defenses. The group is also targeting airports in the south
and east. The Houthis have declared Saudi airspace and airports as theaters of operations,
with the exception, they say, of airports for Mecca and Medina. The attacks come as
Saudi forces and their Yemeni government allies carry out hundreds of airstrikes and attacks
on the Houthis to try and recapture Yemeni territory along the Red Sea.
Ayyeb Etrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
The Vatican says Pope Leo will undergo surgery this week to remove a small growth on his
lung. Megan Williams reports that doctors found the nodule during a routine medical
check-up.
Pope Leo told pilgrims gathered in St. Peter's Square on Sunday that doctors had found what
he called a localized nodule in his lung. He said it was detected at a very early stage
and is well-contained. But doctors recommended removing it. The Vatican says the surgery
will take place in the coming days, with Leo expected to recover in about a week. It's
the first known health scare for the American Pope since his election last year. Leo is
physically active and plays tennis regularly. Next month, he's due to make a 12-day trip
to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru, where he lived for two decades and holds citizenship.
The Vatican has not said whether the surgery will affect those plans. For NPR News, I'm
Megan Williams in Rome.
New inflation numbers are due out this week. NPR's Stephen Besaha reports the data will
be closely watched by investors trying to guess if the Fed will raise rates again.
The Federal Reserve's Preferred Inflation Index showed that inflation came in lower than
expected for August. But Fed Chair Kevin Worsch has said they don't rely on any one figure,
so if September's Consumer Price Index comes in hot, that would add pressure for the Fed
to raise rates later this month. The CPI comes out Wednesday. Before that, on Tuesday, we'll
get September's existing home sales from the National Association of Realtors. Sales
cooled in August due to high mortgage rates. Rates have only gone up sharply since then.
Last week, the average for the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 7.4 percent.
Stephen Besaha, NPR News, Birmingham, Alabama.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Major League Baseball's National League Championship Series gets underway tonight as the Los Angeles
Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers begin a best-of-seven matchup. From Milwaukee, Chuck Kornbach has
a preview of the game.
The Brewers had the best record during baseball's regular season, but the Dodgers swept Milwaukee
during last year's NL Championship and have won two straight World Series. Still, Brewers
fan Luann Andrews says her underdog small market team can win.
Well, you know, David did take down Goliath, so we will take down the Dodgers.
Some baseball analysts say another World Championship for the Dodgers and their high payroll would
lead to more talk of a salary cap during an expected labor dispute this winter.
For NPR News, I'm Chuck Kornbach in Milwaukee.
The Justice Department is investigating whether five major television networks violated antitrust
laws. ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox and NBC temporarily suspended their shared White House coverage
last month. The move came when the administration barred CNN, MS Now and Politico from White
House grounds. The department says coordinated boycotts among business competitors can violate
federal law. Pull coverage resumed when a judge ordered the outlet's access restored.
The network shared the cost of coverage, taking turns providing video to other news outlets.
I'm Windsor Johnston and PR News in Washington.
